title: Fire party communication
goal: Pass messages to the bridge on the radio, read back pressure, and report that a fire is out.

l25-01.text: Fire! Fire in the galley! The pan is on fire!
l25-01.es: ¡Fuego! ¡Fuego en la cocina! ¡La sartén se prendió fuego!

l25-02.text: Fire, fire, fire. This is not a drill. Fire in the galley, main deck. Fire party to the scene. All other crew to the muster station.
l25-02.es: Fuego, fuego, fuego. Esto no es un zafarrancho. Fuego en la cocina, cubierta principal. Brigada de incendio a la escena. El resto de la tripulación al punto de reunión.

l25-03.text: Diego, you're with me. Take a radio. You're my messenger to the bridge.
l25-03.es: Diego, venís conmigo. Agarrá un handy. Sos mi mensajero con el puente.

l25-04.text: Yes, Second. I'll take the radio.

l25-05.text: Mario, did you use the fire blanket?

l25-06.text: Yes, but the fire broke out again, up in the extractor. Too much smoke.
l25-06.es: Sí, pero el fuego se volvió a desatar, arriba en el extractor. Demasiado humo.

l25-07.text: Team one, Rolando and Santos, ready to enter?
l25-07.es: Equipo uno, Rolando y Santos, ¿listos para entrar?

l25-08.text: Team one ready. BA on, pressure two hundred bar.
l25-08.es: Equipo uno listo. Equipos puestos, presión doscientos bar.

l25-09.text: Bridge, fire party. Team one is entering the galley. Over.
l25-09.es: Puente, brigada. El equipo uno está entrando a la cocina. Cambio.

l25-10.text: Team two, start boundary cooling on the galley bulkhead, and back up team one.
l25-10.es: Equipo dos, empiecen el enfriamiento de límites en el mamparo de la cocina, y apoyen al equipo uno.

l25-11.text: Team one at the extractor. Small fire. We're putting it out with CO2.
l25-11.es: Equipo uno en el extractor. Fuego chico. Lo estamos apagando con CO2.

l25-12.text: Bridge, fire party. Team one is at the extractor. Small fire. Over.
l25-12.es: Puente, brigada. El equipo uno está en el extractor. Fuego chico. Cambio.

l25-13.text: Thanks, Diego. Team one, check your pressure. Over.
l25-13.es: Gracias, Diego. Equipo uno, controlen su presión. Cambio.

l25-14.text: Pressure one hundred and forty bar. The fire is out. Repeat, the fire is out.
l25-14.es: Presión ciento cuarenta bar. El fuego está apagado. Repito, el fuego está apagado.

l25-15.text: Bridge, fire party. The fire in the galley is out and contained. No injuries. Boundary cooling continues. Over.
l25-15.es: Puente, brigada de incendio. El fuego en la cocina está apagado y contenido. Sin heridos. El enfriamiento sigue. Cambio.

l25-16.text: Received. Well done, everybody. Keep a fire watch for one hour. Over.
l25-16.es: Recibido. Bien hecho, todos. Mantengan una guardia de incendio por una hora. Cambio.

l25-17.text: Good work, Diego. The bridge knew everything, all the time.
l25-17.es: Buen trabajo, Diego. El puente supo todo, todo el tiempo.

x-fireparty.es: Brigada de incendio a la escena.

x-boundary.text: Start boundary cooling on the bulkhead.

x-mask.text: Check the face mask before you enter.
x-mask.es: Revisá la máscara antes de entrar.

x-radio.text: Take the red radio for the fire party.
x-radio.es: Llevá el handy rojo de la brigada de incendio.

x-torch.text: Take a torch. There is a lot of smoke.
x-torch.es: Llevá una linterna. Hay mucho humo.

p-backup.text: Team two, back up team one.
p-backup.es: Equipo dos, apoyen al equipo uno.

m-out.text: Bridge, the fire is out. No injuries.
m-out.es: Puente, el fuego está apagado. Sin heridos.

c-take.text: Diego, you're with me. Take a radio.

c-report.text: Fire party, bridge. What's the situation? Over.

c-out-other.text: Pressure one hundred and twenty bar. The fire is out.

p-relay.text: Bridge, fire party. Team one is entering the galley. Over.
p-relay.es: Puente, brigada. El equipo uno está entrando a la cocina. Cambio.

m-relay.text: Bridge, fire party. Team two is starting boundary cooling. Over.
m-relay.es: Puente, brigada. El equipo dos empieza a enfriar el mamparo. Cambio.

m-noinj.text: Bridge, fire party. No injuries. Over.

c-relay.text: Diego, tell the bridge: team two is starting boundary cooling.

c-bridge-q.text: Fire party, bridge. Is anybody injured? Over.

c-relay-other.text: Diego, tell the bridge the fire door is closed.

screens.es: Escuchá primero. El texto está escondido a propósito.

screens.title: Three phrasal verbs for fire
steps: A fire broke out in the galley. (empezar de golpe)
We're putting it out with CO2. The fire is out. (apagar)
Team two, back up team one. (apoyar, respaldar)
paras: A phrasal verb is a verb + a small word, and the meaning changes: put is poner, but put out is apagar.
The fire is out is the sentence everybody wants to hear. Say it twice on the radio.
screens.avoid: The fire is off · We're putting off the fire

screens.q: The fire has stopped completely. You say…
A fire started suddenly in the engine room. A fire…
Team two, back up team one.

screens.title: Bridge, fire party: who you call goes first
paras: On the radio you say first who you call, then who you are: Bridge, fire party. Then the message, and Over.
Not Here fire party (aquí brigada), not Hello bridge. And the numbers in English: two hundred bar, not bares.
screens.avoid: Here fire party. · Hello bridge, we are the fire party. · two hundred bars

screens.q: What does James want you to tell the bridge?
What's the pressure now?

screens.title: bar, BA, over
paras: bar: one short syllable, no s in the plural: two hundred bar.
BA: letter by letter, bee-AY. Over at the end, clear: OH-ver.
